name: Google Calendar
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Display upcoming events from Google Calendar with date, time, and event details. Shows next 1-3 events with automatic rotation and timezone support.

web_ui_actions.title: Step 2: Authenticate with Google
web_ui_actions.description: Click to generate an authorization link. Visit the link in your browser, authorize access, then paste the code back here.
web_ui_actions.step2_prompt: Paste the authorization code from Google:

versions.notes: Documentation. The README's three ASCII mock-ups of the display are replaced with real rendered screenshots of the same four screens (timed, all-day, a long title being ellipsized, and the empty state) plus a panel-size sheet. Documents google_auth, which is the web UI's Connect Your Google Account button rather than a value you type, and splits the two combined font rows so each customization key appears on its own. All 13 schema settings are now documented by key.

Restores the minimum-core requirement that 1.2.0 declared. That release added the device-authorization step to the setup flow and needs the calendar_registration endpoints the core gained after 3.2.0, so it floored at 3.3.0. The two bug-fix releases after it, 1.2.1 and 1.2.2, each wrote a fresh versions[] entry declaring 2.0.0 -- and because the core reads the floor from versions[0] alone, the requirement disappeared the moment 1.2.1 shipped. A floor is cumulative: the feature that needs the newer core is still in the plugin. The store will now refuse to install this on a core older than 3.3.0 rather than handing over a setup flow whose Step 2 cannot work.

versions.changelog: Fixes the event display pulsing: the plugin cleared the physical panel before every frame it rendered, so the display went black between redraws. Frames are now composed off-panel and swapped in.

versions.notes: Ignore credentials.json and token.pickle in the plugin .gitignore so local Google OAuth artifacts cannot be committed by accident.

Add the missing Step 2 to the setup. The config advertised Step 1 (upload credentials) and Step 3 (pick calendars) with nothing between them, so there was no way to actually authorize the device from the web UI -- and Step 3 could only ever fail, since it needs the token Step 2 produces. calendar_registration.py already handled this flow; it simply had no field to drive it. Requires the core endpoints from LEDMatrix#458; the floor assumes they ship in 3.3.0, the next minor after the current 3.2.0.

Fix Google Calendar auth failing with 'invalid_grant: Missing code verifier'. The web-UI flow runs as two separate processes, but the PKCE code_verifier generated while building the auth URL was never carried into the token-exchange step. It is now persisted between the two steps (and cleaned up afterward).

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.

Fix event titles silently dropping trailing wrapped lines on narrow panels (e.g. 'Team Standup Meeting' showed only 'Team'/'Standup' at 64x32, with no sign 'Meeting' ever existed) -- the last visible line now ellipsizes ('Stan...') instead. Also brightened the 'No Events' fallback text from a dim (150,150,150) to (220,220,220) for better contrast.

Document the config in a per-key table (including the previously-undocumented customization fonts), add web-UI titles to the untitled options (Max Events, Show All-Day Events, durations, Update Interval), and normalize the versions changelog key to ledmatrix_min_version.
